title: APN-permutation nonexistence in five small-dimensional LE classes
summary: Decide whether the five unexhausted linear-self-equivalence classes in dimensions seven and eight contain no APN permutations.

formal_statement.body: For the source-listed linear-self-equivalence cases, decide whether any associated permutation $F$ satisfying $F\circ A=B\circ F$ can be APN. The five cases are Classes $16,22,23$ in dimension $7$ and Classes $22,30$ in dimension $8$. Prove nonexistence of APN permutations in all five cases, or exhibit an APN permutation in at least one case.

scope.domain: The five finite linear-self-equivalence cases left unexhausted by the source classification
assumptions: Each class uses the source-listed canonical pair $(B,A)$
$F$ is a permutation satisfying $F\circ A=B\circ F$
parameters: permutation $F$ in the corresponding self-equivalence subspace
scope.unresolved_remainder: Settle all five finite cases by proving that each contains no APN permutation, or provide a verified APN-permutation witness in any one case.

citations.label: Kuznetsov, partial Groebner search in dimension-eight Class 22
citations.locator: arXiv v2, 428 of 65,536 slices (0.65%); all 566 found APN functions are non-permutations

progress.summary: The source isolates three seven-dimensional and two eight-dimensional linear-self-equivalence classes whose APN-permutation status remains unexhausted.
Kuznetsov searches 428 of 65,536 slices in the dimension-eight Class-22 subspace and finds only APN non-permutations; the remaining 99.35% and the other four classes remain unsettled.
